steps.text: Rinse and cook the rice.
steps.narration: Start the rice first, since it can cook while you do everything else.

detail.how: Rinse the grains under cold water until the water running off them is clear rather than cloudy, then cook them however you normally would. A short or medium grain works well here because it stays soft in the fridge all week.
detail.watch_for: Measuring short. Cooked rice keeps well, and leftovers become fried rice.

steps.text: Trim and halve the brussels sprouts.
steps.narration: Cut the stems off the sprouts and halve them.

detail.how: Slice the dry stem end off each sprout, then cut it in half from top to bottom. Any outer leaves that are browned or gritty will fall away on their own once the stem goes; discard those.
detail.watch_for: Leaving the tough stem on, which stays hard even after roasting.

steps.text: Toss the sprouts with oil, salt and pepper.
steps.narration: Coat the halved sprouts in a little oil and season them.

steps.text: Air fry the sprouts in a single layer at 400F / 204C for 5 to 8 minutes.
steps.narration: Air fry the sprouts until the edges catch colour.

detail.how: Spread them across the basket in one layer so hot air reaches every surface. With no air fryer, spread them on a sheet pan and roast at the same temperature, allowing noticeably longer.
detail.watch_for: Piling them up. Crowded sprouts steam and turn soft instead of browning.
detail.duration_hint: 5 to 8 minutes in an air fryer, closer to 20 in an oven.

steps.text: Dice the green onions and the sweet onion.
steps.narration: Cut the green onion tops small for garnish, and dice the sweet onion.

steps.text: Dice the poblano peppers.
steps.narration: Cut the poblanos into a small dice.

detail.how: Halve each pepper and cut it into strips, then across into a small dice that matches the onion. The seeds and pale ribs carry nearly all the heat, so scrape them out for a mild dish or leave some in for warmth.
detail.watch_for: Poblanos are mild to begin with. A green bell pepper substitutes fine if you cannot find them.

steps.text: Cut the lime into small wedges.
steps.narration: Quarter the lime, then halve each wedge.

steps.text: Soften the onion and peppers in a hot skillet.
steps.narration: Get a large pan hot over medium-high and add the onion and peppers with a little oil.

steps.text: Add the red pepper flakes, then the minced garlic.
steps.narration: Stir the chilli flakes through, then drop the garlic into the middle of the pan.

steps.text: Season the vegetables and the beef with salt and pepper.
steps.narration: Give the vegetables a pinch of salt and season the beef.

detail.how: A pinch of salt on the vegetables pulls their water out so they soften rather than fry. Season the raw beef at the same time so you are not doing it later with a full pan.
detail.watch_for: Salting nothing until the end, which leaves the vegetables bland under the sauce.

steps.text: Push the vegetables to the edge and brown the beef in the middle.
steps.narration: Clear the centre of the pan and add the beef to brown.

detail.how: Press the beef into the cleared centre so as much of it as possible touches the hot metal, and leave it alone for a minute before breaking it up. Cooking it in a separate pan browns it better, at the cost of washing up.
detail.watch_for: Stirring straight away. Beef that is constantly moved releases water and grey-steams instead of browning.

steps.text: Whisk together the honey, hot sauce and apple cider vinegar.
steps.narration: Mix the sauce while the beef cooks.

steps.text: Whisk the cornstarch into the sauce.
steps.narration: Stir the cornstarch in until it disappears.

detail.how: Stir the cornstarch into a spoonful of cold water first, then add that slurry to the sauce. Dropping dry starch straight into liquid is what makes lumps that never dissolve.
detail.watch_for: Lumps. If you get them, keep stirring; they break down eventually but slowly.

steps.text: Pour the sauce in once the beef is nearly cooked through.
steps.narration: When the beef is about ninety percent done, stir the sauce and pour it into the pan.

steps.text: Add the sprouts and stir until everything is coated.
steps.narration: Tip the air-fried sprouts in and fold everything together.

detail.how: Keep folding until the sauce clings to the beef and coats the cut faces of the sprouts. If it has tightened too much, loosen it with water a splash at a time.
detail.watch_for: Adding too much water at once. You can always add more, never take it back.

steps.text: Taste and adjust the seasoning.
steps.narration: Taste it and add more salt, pepper or chilli flakes if it needs them.

steps.text: Portion 3/4 cup (112 g) of rice into each of five containers.
steps.narration: Lay out five containers and spread rice across the base of each.

steps.text: Divide the beef and sprouts between the containers.
steps.narration: Share the beef and sprouts evenly over the rice.

detail.how: For portions that match exactly, weigh the whole pan and divide by five. Scooping by eye is close enough if you are eating all five yourself.
detail.watch_for: Loading the first containers heavily and running short at the end.

steps.text: Top each with green onion and a lime wedge.
steps.narration: Finish each container with green onion and a wedge of lime.

steps.text: Cool, lid and refrigerate for up to five days.
steps.narration: Let them cool before putting the lids on, then refrigerate.

detail.how: Leave the containers open until they are near room temperature, otherwise trapped steam condenses and waterlogs the rice. Reheat in the microwave, stirring every 30 seconds until hot through.
detail.watch_for: Sealing them while warm. Squeeze the lime over just before eating, not before storing.

title: Sheet Pan Protein Pancakes & Taco Mac

steps.text: Blend the milk, applesauce, cottage cheese, maple syrup and vanilla.
steps.narration: Blend the wet ingredients for the pancakes together.

detail.how: Run the blender until the mixture is completely smooth and no grains of cottage cheese remain. Those curds are what carry the protein, and any you leave whole will show up as lumps in the finished pancake.
detail.watch_for: Stopping too early. Hold it up to the light before you decide it is smooth.

steps.text: Whisk the egg whites until frothy.
steps.narration: Whip the egg whites until they foam and grow in volume.

steps.text: Combine the oat flour, powdered milk, salt, baking powder and baking soda.
steps.narration: Mix all the dry ingredients together until no clumps are left.

steps.text: Fold the blended mixture into the egg whites.
steps.narration: Pour the blender contents into the whipped whites and combine them gently.

detail.how: Pour slowly and turn the mixture over rather than beating it, so the air you just whipped into the whites survives. That trapped air is what makes the baked sheet rise instead of sitting flat.
detail.watch_for: Stirring hard and knocking all the volume back out.

steps.text: Whisk in the dry ingredients to make the batter.
steps.narration: Add the dry mix in slowly and whisk to a batter.

steps.text: Divide the batter between two lined sheet pans and level it.
steps.narration: Split the batter across two parchment-lined, oiled sheet pans.

steps.text: Bake at 375F / 190C for about 20 minutes.
steps.narration: Bake the pancake sheets while you start the taco mac.

steps.text: Chop the green onions, keeping the whites and greens apart.
steps.narration: Cut the green onions up, separating whites from greens into two piles.

detail.how: The white and pale green parts go into the pot to cook down with the beef; the dark green tops stay raw and go on top at the end for colour.
detail.watch_for: Mixing the two piles, which costs you the garnish.

steps.text: Dice the bell peppers to match the onion.
steps.narration: Deseed the peppers and dice them the same size as the onion.

steps.text: Brown the ground beef in a large pot with a spoon of oil.
steps.narration: Heat oil in a large pot and cook the seasoned beef until it colours.

detail.how: Let the beef sit undisturbed for a few minutes to take on colour before you break it apart, then keep breaking it down as it finishes. Extra-lean beef works here because the sauce keeps it from drying out.
detail.watch_for: Breaking it up immediately, which draws out water and prevents any browning.

steps.text: Add the onion whites and peppers and cook until softened.
steps.narration: Stir the onions and peppers in and let them soften with the beef.

steps.text: Stir in the spices and let them bloom for a minute or two.
steps.narration: Add the chilli powder, paprika, garlic powder, cumin and onion powder, and stir to coat the meat.

detail.how: Keep everything moving over the heat for a minute or two once the spices are in. Warming ground spices in fat draws out flavour that never appears if they are simply stirred into liquid.
detail.watch_for: Letting them catch on a dry pan, which turns them bitter fast.

steps.text: Add the crushed tomatoes and beef broth.
steps.narration: Pour in the crushed tomatoes and the beef broth.

steps.text: Stir in the macaroni, keeping it under the liquid.
steps.narration: Add the dried macaroni and stir it through.

steps.text: Bring to a light boil, cover, and cook on low for 10 to 12 minutes.
steps.narration: Bring it up to a gentle boil, put the lid on and turn the heat down.

detail.how: A few noodles sitting above the liquid is fine; the trapped steam cooks them, and a stir partway through rotates them down into the sauce.
detail.watch_for: A hard boil with the lid on, which catches starch on the base of the pot.

steps.text: Stir at around eight minutes and test a noodle.
steps.narration: Stir the pot partway through and taste a piece of pasta for doneness.

detail.how: Fish out a single noodle and bite it. Gluten-free pasta is the one to watch: it softens faster than wheat and will break down into the sauce if you leave it too long.
detail.watch_for: Going by the clock instead of tasting.

steps.text: Take it off the heat, stir in the milk, then taste and season.
steps.narration: Cut the heat, pour the milk in and stir, then adjust the salt and pepper.

detail.how: The milk goes in after the boiling is finished. Dairy proteins split into grainy curds if they are boiled in an acidic tomato sauce, and off the heat they simply loosen everything into a creamy finish.
detail.watch_for: Adding the milk while it is still bubbling.

steps.text: Divide into five containers and top with cheese and green onion.
steps.narration: Split the pot between five containers, then scatter cheese and the green onion tops over each.

steps.text: Cool, lid and refrigerate for up to five days.
steps.narration: Let everything stop steaming before you put the lids on, then refrigerate.

detail.how: Reheat in the microwave for two to three minutes, stirring about once a minute so the pasta in the middle heats through as fast as the edges.
detail.watch_for: Sealing hot containers, which leaves condensation in the sauce.

steps.text: Slice the pancake sheets into 24 pieces and freeze them.
steps.narration: Cut each cooled pancake tray into twelve slices and freeze them.

detail.how: Spread the slices out to freeze solid before bagging them, so they do not fuse into one block. Reheat in the microwave, or in an air fryer if you want the edges crisp.
detail.watch_for: Bagging them while soft.

steps.text: Rinse and cook the rice.
steps.narration: Get the rice going first so it cooks while you work.

steps.text: Stir the marinade together into a paste.
steps.narration: In a large bowl, mix the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, chilli powder, salt and pepper with lime juice, oil and a spoon of water.

detail.how: Add the liquids to the dry spices and stir until you have a loose paste rather than a powder. The water is there to let the ground spices absorb moisture so they cling to the meat instead of falling off it.
detail.watch_for: Leaving it powdery, which gives you patchy seasoning.

steps.text: Coat the chicken thighs in the marinade.
steps.narration: Add the thighs and turn them until every surface is covered.

detail.how: Work the paste into every fold of each thigh. Thighs are the right cut for food you will microwave later, because their extra fat keeps them tender well past the point where breast meat would go dry and stringy.
detail.watch_for: Using breast instead; it overcooks easily and reheats poorly.

steps.text: Bake the chicken at 400F / 204C for 22 to 25 minutes.
steps.narration: Lay the thighs smooth side down on a lightly oiled sheet tray and bake.

steps.text: Dice the sweet potato into 1/4 to 1/2 inch cubes.
steps.narration: Cut the sweet potato into small even cubes.

steps.text: Cut the broccoli into small florets.
steps.narration: Break the broccoli down into small pieces.

detail.how: Turn each head upside down and cut up through the stalk rather than across the top. Slicing horizontally through the florets shears off the buds and leaves you with a pile of crumbs. Any stalk you keep should be chopped small so it cooks in the same time as the florets.
detail.watch_for: Thick stalk pieces staying raw while the florets scorch.

steps.text: Roughly chop the green onions for the sauce.
steps.narration: Chop the green onions so the blender can catch them.

steps.text: Toss the sweet potato with oil and salt and spread it on a sheet pan.
steps.narration: Coat the potato cubes in oil, season, and spread them out.

steps.text: Roast the sweet potato for 10 to 15 minutes.
steps.narration: Put the potatoes into the oven for their first stint.

steps.text: Blend the sauce.
steps.narration: Into a blender put the green onion, jalapeno, cilantro, garlic powder, cumin, salt, lime juice, oil and Greek yogurt.

detail.how: Tear the cilantro up before it goes in, so long stems cannot wrap themselves around the blade and stall the machine. Blend until the herbs disappear into the yogurt and the whole thing turns pale green.
detail.watch_for: Stems tangling the blade and leaving the sauce chunky.

steps.text: Thin the sauce with water until it pours.
steps.narration: Check the consistency and loosen it with a little water.

detail.how: You are aiming for something that falls off a spoon like a salad dressing rather than sitting on it like a dip. Add water a tablespoon at a time and blend briefly between additions.
detail.watch_for: Overshooting. A watery sauce runs straight off the rice.

steps.text: Toss the potatoes, push them to one side and add the broccoli.
steps.narration: Pull the tray out, turn the potatoes over and make room on one half.

steps.text: Toss the broccoli with oil and salt and roast for another 10 to 12 minutes.
steps.narration: Coat the broccoli the same way and return the tray to the oven.

steps.text: Pull the chicken out and let it rest.
steps.narration: Take the chicken tray out and set it aside.

steps.text: Divide the sauce between five ramekins.
steps.narration: Share the sauce out into five small pots so it travels separately.

steps.text: Chop the rested chicken into a medium dice.
steps.narration: Move the chicken to a board and cut it into chunks.

steps.text: Pour the rendered chicken juices over the broccoli, then taste and season.
steps.narration: Tip the juices left on the chicken tray over the roasted broccoli, mix, and adjust the seasoning.

detail.how: Those juices are fat and browned meat drippings that would otherwise go in the bin, and they cost nothing extra since the chicken is already counted in the portion. Poured over the broccoli and mixed through, they season it better than more salt would.
detail.watch_for: Washing the tray before you have used them.

steps.text: Divide the rice between five containers.
steps.narration: Spread the cooked rice evenly across five containers.

steps.text: Add a fifth of the potato, broccoli and chicken to each, with a pot of sauce.
steps.narration: Portion the vegetables and chicken over the rice and add a ramekin of sauce to each.

steps.text: Cool, lid and refrigerate for up to five days.
steps.narration: Once cooled, put the lids on and move them to the fridge.

detail.how: Keep the sauce in its own pot rather than dressing the bowls now, so it stays fresh and cold and does not soak into the rice over five days. Tip it over just before eating and mix everything together.
detail.watch_for: Dressing the bowls in advance.
